touches.text: Questions live here and nowhere else. The questions/ inbox and `cairn question` are deprecated for now. -amm

An artifact is present tense or past tense, never both. Present tense is rewritten whole and points at its provenance; past tense is append-only, opened when needed, and read cold only through a compiled face (state, the latest slate). WHY: what a cold reader loads at an address should be what is true now.
A dated aside (retired, formerly, a date in parentheses) in a present-tense artifact is history in the wrong place, and reads red. -akiendelllinux_cc_0

The plan is <id>-<slug>.json: current, one-line outcomes and constraints. The history is <id>.log.jsonl, append-only. Questions live in the outline (0.6.2). A big decision goes in these files; a small one on the ticket.

question: the open-question door: a decision only the operator can make, bound to its ticket, answered in the operator's words. WHY: a spec choice is settled by Akien's head, recorded verbatim, never by a paragraph of CC's. USERS: tickets and CodeMother open them; the operator answers (7.4.2).

dataref: one address for any stored record, in any format, and the thin class that reads it. WHY: a config, a ticket or a node can say WHERE a value lives without carrying it, so the repo stays shareable and a private value stays in ~/.cairn; and one way of pointing works across every format and every box. USERS: anything that reads stored data.

A file Dataref keeps its value and re-reads only when the file's modification time, size or inode has changed (a stat reads no data; a write that replaces the file in one step gets a new inode, which catches a change where timestamps are coarse). A Secret keeps nothing between reads. A db Dataref does not cache until a measured need asks for it. HYPOTHESIS: it will be read often enough for the cache to pay; the reads are counted (a metric, 17.27) to find out.
One that does not resolve is loud and names its address, never a value. A sieve reds a class-space config holding a plain value where a secret belongs.

A secret is marked when the need for it is created, not by a list or a key's name: the day a secret comes into being, its value goes into its holder's env file and the code names its key there, and from that day every use of it is a secret: address, so the factory hands back a Secret (17.28.2). The place a secret belongs is wherever such a key is used; a plain value there is the red. WHY: the need for a secret is what makes it one, as with CC's own email address: the day it was made, its values went in CC's env file and its keys into the code.

QUESTIONS: a question is [Q#n: ...], placed at the line it bears on. Its #n is its own and never changes; a new one takes the next unused number, which is now 127. An answered question disappears: its answer is folded into the intention and why (0.2.1), and signed where it records a decision (0.5). Why? Becuase too many words makes it hard for both akien and Claude to understand.
Proofs run against a TESTING database, separate from live.

A Dataref reads; it never writes. A write goes through the owner's gate (Law 6), and a db: address is read through db_domain's own client, never a second dial to 5432. An address on another box is read over the bus. WHY: one address system must not become one back door.

Ideas and questions are not tickets. An idea is a note that leads to an intention, and stops mattering once the intention is set down. A question exists only to deduce the why: once answered, what matters is the answer and the why, and nothing else.
Knowledge: one list of nodes, owned by the librarian.

The memory model. Everything Cairn keeps as LEARNING in database memory is these five things, and only these. Logs, troubles, git records and a device's own state keep their own homes (4.3.2-4.3.4). WHY: one kind of access everywhere.

Cross-domain questions (cognition questions): inherently cross domain, not domain specific. "How might that work?" is Akien's number one: it applies in almost every domain, and captures the pattern rather than the domain's answer. They are not design questions: a design question is a spec choice waiting on Akien (a [Q#n] in the outline, 0.6.2).

Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a [Q#n] at the outline line it bears on (0.6.2), and that open [Q#n] holds the ticket's build until it is answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing. WHY: a ticket that contradicts the outline builds something Akien did not intend, and the cheapest time to catch that is before the build. - CC

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.
